posts.title: Volume is not stakes (ADP/Valence)
posts.hook: I've been sitting with a split I keep seeing in the rooms and in the research I read for work.
posts.caption:
I've been sitting with a split I keep seeing in the rooms and in the research I read for work.

On one side: AI coaching is getting real capital and real distribution. ADP Ventures put money into Valence after a pilot past a thousand users and tens of thousands of coaching interactions. Conversation volume is starting to look like a product metric. That layer matters. Fluency at scale is a real job.

On the other side: leaders still show up carrying board-adjacent calls with incomplete information, team freezes no curriculum names, or a life question wearing a performance jacket. Those hours do not compress cleanly into interaction counts.

I used to feel pressure to pick a tribe. Scale story or depth story.

I don't anymore. Different jobs. I respect the volume layer. I choose the hours where complexity is the brief, not the obstacle. Whole person. High touch. Movement after truth.

If you buy or lead above the director line, fund the layer that matches the weight you are actually carrying.

#executivecoaching #leadershipdevelopment #AIcoaching

posts.title: Green boxes, dirty problem
posts.hook: A leader came in with a clean deck and a dirty problem.
posts.caption:
A leader came in with a clean deck and a dirty problem.

Every box on the transformation plan was green. Sponsors were getting updates. The team was "aligned" in every forum that required a slide. Nothing that mattered was actually moving.

We didn't fix the deck. We sat with the sentence he had been avoiding: he was performing progress for the system, because real progress would force a conflict he did not want to own yet.

Once that was named, the work got simpler and harder at the same time. One decision. One conversation. One person who had been protected by the theater.

I read a lot about content, modules, and AI practice reps right now. Some of that is useful. Skill gaps are real.

What I care about when I close the laptop after a session is narrower.

Did we produce movement, or evidence of movement?

Those are not the same craft.

#executivecoaching #leadership #change

posts.title: Work that holds on Friday afternoon
posts.hook: When I was leading teams inside Fortune 500 transformations, the plan was rarely what kept me up.
posts.caption:
When I was leading teams inside Fortune 500 transformations, the plan was rarely what kept me up.

What kept me up was whether the work would hold when a real customer, a real peer, or a real sponsor pushed back. Pretty problem statements died in those rooms. So did clever frameworks that could not survive a Friday afternoon.

I still coach for that test.

With leaders and cohorts now, we push past theory into application: clear problem and solution statements, decision quality, operating metrics, risk and gaps. I read the room fast, challenge what is avoided, and keep checking whether the session is hitting the real goal. Then we adjust. Not stuck to a script.

Home taught me the same thing quieter. Attention is finite. If I give the polished version of myself to work and the leftovers to the people I love, both places feel it. Integration is not a soft category. It is how decision quality stays honest.

I don't coach the title. I coach the whole person who showed up, because that is who has to execute when the room gets sharp.

#leadership #executivecoaching #wholeperson

posts.title: Package altitude is the first sale
posts.hook: Here's something I keep relearning in commercial and design rooms.
posts.caption:
Here's something I keep relearning in commercial and design rooms.

The first failure in leadership development is often not weak content. It is buying the wrong package for the actual problem.

Benefit portal seats, academy pathways, private cohorts, closed cohorts of an open program, full custom. Different mechanisms. Different sponsors. Different success dashboards. If you skip package altitude and jump to modules and brand names, you get scope thrash and a sponsor who cannot defend the buy six months later.

I have watched serious buyers lock business priority first: profit, cost, or risk. Then what leaders must do differently. Then metrics. Then design. The ones who start with a faculty wish list and "we need a leadership program" usually buy recognition. That can be valid. It is not the same purchase as transformation.

I sit closer to private-cohort and high-stakes human work on purpose. Intact teams. Sponsor-tied application. Rooms where judgment under pressure is the constraint, not seat count.

Name the package before you fall in love with the syllabus.

#leadershipdevelopment #executiveeducation #CHRO

posts.title: Not only her capability
posts.hook: A company sent me a high-performing director and called it a leadership problem.
posts.caption:
A company sent me a high-performing director and called it a leadership problem.

She was sharp. Willing. Already carrying more than her title suggested. By session two it was obvious the bottleneck was not her capability. It was a leadership team that could not make a clean decision without reopening it three forums later.

We still did the individual work. Identity, presence, how she was landing. We also named the system she was being asked to outrun alone.

Individual certificates without team-level change are a common buy. Sometimes they help. Often they become a private gym membership next to a broken operating rhythm.

I care about the person in the chair. I also care whether the team can execute after the insight lands. Otherwise we did theater with better language.

If you sponsor development, ask what has to change in the room around them, not only in them.

#teamcoaching #executivecoaching #leadership

posts.title: Stress as climate
posts.caption:
Here's something I wrestle with.

The field keeps publishing what a lot of us already feel in our bodies. Leaders under rising stress. Thin bench confidence. Frontline managers more afraid of AI obsolescence than the people above them. CHROs trying to fund readiness while cost optimization sits near the top of the enterprise stack.

I don't doubt the numbers. I doubt our response.

More content is the easy answer. More AI practice is the fashionable one. Both can help at the right layer. Neither automatically builds a leader who can stay human while the system tightens.

What I trust more, slowly, is relationship dense enough for the real sentence. The one under the performance narrative. The one that explains why a capable person goes still, or leaves, or performs green while the work dies.

I do not have a clean product SKU for that. I have a choice about where I put my hours.

If you lead people right now, what are you building that still works when the stress is not a quarter, but a climate?

#leadership #executivecoaching #workforce

posts.title: CHRO agenda placement
posts.hook: The CHRO agenda I keep hearing is not mysterious.
posts.caption:
The CHRO agenda I keep hearing is not mysterious.

Leader and manager development still sits first. Change management and workforce resiliency climbed. HR tech and AI strategy jumped once people stopped treating them as separate hobbies. Culture remains near the top. Engagement, as a lead frame, lost altitude.

That map matters if you do senior human work for a living.

I work where organizations are already investing: leader and manager development, change and resiliency, and the human side of HR tech and AI strategy. Not as a content library. As applied work with leaders, teams, and cohorts who need movement, not theater.

Over 1,500 hours with 250+ senior leaders and founders, globally, has not made me romantic about any of this. It has made me practical. Decision quality. Operating metrics. Risk and gaps. Work that holds when a customer, peer, or sponsor pushes back.

If you own that agenda, the useful split is still the same. Scale where scale fits. Depth where depth is the actual requirement.

#CHRO #leadershipdevelopment #executivecoaching

posts.title: Wrong layer (quiet door)
posts.hook: The costliest development mistake I see is not hiring the wrong person.
posts.caption:
The costliest development mistake I see is not hiring the wrong person.

It is buying the wrong layer of help for the actual problem.

A manager drowning in new scope often needs structured skill, feedback loops, and practice reps. Scaled support, including AI-assisted practice, can serve that well.

A VP who looks composed in every forum and cannot sleep because the role and the rest of their life are no longer the same person needs something else. A relationship sturdy enough for an inconvenient truth. Slower. Not a five-module fix.

I coach that second category on purpose. Whole person. Not title only. Movement after truth.

If you are a senior leader carrying more than your org chart shows, or you sponsor someone who is, you already know which layer you are in.
